entries.principle_source: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence, OECD/LEGAL/0449 (2019, amended 2024), principle 1.4
entries.provision: Art. 5(1)(d), accuracy principle; used as a benchmark, the fictional fund is not established in the EU
entries.why_here: Part 4 showed the bare pipeline rejected a profile with GPA 9.9 and exam score -5 instead of flagging broken data, so a decision was made on inaccurate personal data.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (2021), section III.2, 'Fairness and non-discrimination'
entries.instrument: Constitution of the Republic of Kazakhstan, 30 August 1995
entries.provision: Art. 14(2), no discrimination on grounds including sex, nationality and language
entries.why_here: Part 1 found 4 of 40 gender-coded pairs flipped, all towards the female-coded name, and a +2.5 [+1.1, +4.1] score shift towards flagship universities; neither name nor university is a merit criterion, so the model is not shown them.

entries.principle: Respect for the rule of law, human rights and democratic values, including privacy
entries.principle_source: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence, OECD/LEGAL/0449 (2019, amended 2024), principle 1.2
entries.provision: Art. 5(1)(b), purpose limitation, and Art. 6(1)(a), consent as a lawful basis; used as a benchmark
entries.why_here: Part 4 showed the bare pipeline shortlisted a request to rank applicants by ethnicity and scored an applicant who had not consented, so purposes and inputs outside the system's lawful scope must be stopped before the model sees them.

entries.principle_source: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence, OECD/LEGAL/0449 (2019, amended 2024), principle 1.5
entries.provision: Art. 12, record-keeping (automatic logging) for high-risk AI systems; benchmark, the fund is outside the EU
entries.why_here: With 50 of 400 decisions changing between the bare and the harness run, a reviewer must be able to see afterwards which fields the model saw, what it replied and which control fired, without re-running the model.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (2021), section III.2, 'Human oversight and determination'
entries.provision: Art. 22(1) and 22(3), right not to be subject to a solely automated decision and to obtain human intervention; benchmark
entries.why_here: Part 1 placed the boundary between reject and shortlist near a score of 45, where 33 rejected and 31 shortlisted profiles sat in the 40-49 range, so decisions in that band are uncertain and go to a person; the run sent 38 of 400 (9.5%).
